title: Treasury to Appeal High Court Ruling on Safaricom Stake Sale
desc: Treasury will challenge the High Court ruling that cancelled the government’s 15% Safaricom stake sale to Vodacom, CS John Mbadi says.
content:
The National Treasury will appeal a High Court decision that cancelled the government's sale of a 15 per cent stake in Safaricom to Vodacom, Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi announced on Wednesday, September 16.

Speaking to journalists in Kisumu, Mbadi said the government would challenge the judgment through the Court of Appeal. The announcement comes a day after the High Court ruled against the transaction.

The disputed sale involved 15 per cent of Safaricom and was completed on June 30, 2026, after earlier court proceedings had allowed the transaction to proceed. The transfer increased Vodacom's effective holding in Safaricom to about 55 per cent, while the Kenyan government retained a 20 per cent stake.

On Tuesday, September 15, a three-judge High Court bench declared the divestiture unconstitutional and null and void. The judges ordered the 15 per cent holding to be restored to the Government of Kenya on behalf of the people. The court also quashed decisions and approvals connected to the transaction.

The judgment followed a legal challenge to the way the government handled the sale. The court found that the process failed to satisfy constitutional and legal requirements, including requirements concerning public participation and information surrounding the transaction.

The government now intends to take the dispute to the appellate court rather than accept the High Court's decision as final. The appeal will determine whether the transaction can ultimately stand or whether the High Court's orders will remain in force.

Vodacom is also pursuing an appeal. In a regulatory disclosure dated September 15, the South African telecommunications group said it would lodge an appeal and seek a stay of the judgment while the matter is considered by the Court of Appeal.

Safaricom has meanwhile said it is reviewing the judgment and its implications. The company's position comes as the legal dispute over the 15 per cent stake moves into another stage.

For now, the ownership dispute remains before the courts, with both the Kenyan government and Vodacom preparing to challenge the High Court decision.
